: binds irreversibly to the 30S ribosomal subunit, inhibiting bacterial protein synthesis; bactericidal
•there is a synergistic effect when combined w/ a beta-lactam or Vancomycin
•not good for gram (+) or anaerobic coverage
: slightly increased activity against Pseudomonas; topical use for Keratitis
•ototoxicity (vestibular & cochlear) – cautious use of Gentamicin w/ other ototoxic drugs, such as Cisplatin, Furosemide, Bumetanide, Ethacrynic acid, & high-dose NSAIDs
•neuromuscular paralysis – increased muscular weakness in pts w/ Myasthenia gravis
•reduced activity in sites w/ acidic pH
component of fungal cell membranes and alters permeability to allow leakage of ions and other intracellular components → cell death
May be either fungistatic or fungicidal, depending on tissue concentration achieved and organism susceptibility
: broadest spectrum of coverage of all the antifungals
: infusion reactions (fever/chills, HA, malaise, rigors, BP changes, thrombophlebitis, N/V), nephrotoxicity, decreased K & Mg, anemia, back/chest pain (AmBisome)
: empiric therapy of atypical fungal infections;
: transient visual disturbances (photophobia, blurred vision, color changes), hallucinations

: synthetic purine nucleoside analog with activity against HSV (types 1 and 2), varicella-zoster virus (VZV), and Epstein-Barr virus (EBV); stops replication of herpes viral DNA by competitive inhibition of viral DNA polymerase (selective toxicity), incorporation into and termination of the growing viral DNA chain, and inactivation of the viral DNA polymerase
: IV (injection site inflammation or phlebitis, transient elevation of SCr/BUN, N/V), PO (GI disturbances, HA, skin rash)
: triphosphate form inhibits viral DNA synthesis by competitively inhibiting viral DNA polymerases and by getting incorporated into viral DNA resulting in chain termination
: fever, abdominal pain, GI disturbances, blood dyscrasias, rash, phlebitis/pain at injection site

: closely resembles thymidine (also called trifluorothymidine); trifluridine is incorporated in place of thymidine into viral DNA, resulting in faulty DNA and the inability to reproduce or to infect or destroy tissue
: ophthalmic herpes simplex, primary keratoconjunctivitis, recurrent epithelial keratitis due to HSV1/2
